A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have designed a new peer-to-peer lookup scheme which has a small routing state and a small amount of bookkeeping required to handle system membership changes, while still achieving low latency for lookup operations.

we have designed a novel routing scheme that achieves the best of both worlds: it keeps routing information small and yet achieves very low lookup latency, by exploiting the fact that the network is highly dynamic.
we have developed an algorithm that can be used for efficient routing in peer-to-peer networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the case of small lookup tables, the lookup cost can be reduced to a single message per lookup, while keeping the routing state per member node small.
it may be possible to achieve low-latency lookups with small routing tables.
, in contrast with the current state of the art, it is not necessary to keep routing state small in order to keep bookkeeping low.
